title: Candidaemia and a risk predictive model for overall mortality: a prospective multicentre study.

region_city_raw: New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia and other states (8 hospitals)
sources_raw: C1: blood cultures of adults with candidaemia
species_id_raw: MALDI-TOF MS (Biotyper) or Vitek 2 YST/API 20C AUX/ID 32C; confirmation by ITS sequencing in a reference laboratory
ast_method_raw: performed in a reference laboratory; no results by species

title: Active surveillance for candidemia, Australia.
ft_screening_reason: absolute number of C. tropicalis not reported (percentage only)
extraction_change_reason: DOUBTFUL at screening because C. tropicalis is given only as a %. With the full text the n is calculated: 5.1% of 1068 episodes with identified species = 54.5 (compatible with 54-55); 54 is taken (calculated from %). Meets the rule via IC3 (distribution) without IC4 (no susceptibility by species), as B001.
setting_raw: 50 of 52 public and private microbiology laboratories; hospitals
sources_raw: C1: blood cultures (candidaemia) of adults, children and neonates
population_raw: patients of all ages with candidaemia
species_id_raw: standard phenotypic methods; confirmation in a reference laboratory by conventional methods; PCR for C. dubliniensis
ast_method_raw: sent to a reference laboratory for susceptibility, but results are not reported
azole_exposure_raw: Systemic antifungals in 121 episodes (67 as prophylaxis); not disaggregated by species
extraction_notes: n of C. tropicalis calculated from % (5.1% × 1068; possible range 54-55). 1095 incident episodes; species identified in 1068. No susceptibility data by species. This cohort (2001-2004) is the historical validation series of B001 (no period overlap with B001).

title: Population-Based Active Surveillance for Culture-Confirmed Candidemia - Four Sites, United States, 2012-2016.
journal: Morbidity and mortality weekly report. Surveillance summaries (Washington, D.C. : 2002)
ft_screening_reason: Meets general rule and IC8 (CLSI M27-A3/M27-S4, denominators by antifungal agent)
design_raw: active population-based laboratory surveillance (Emerging Infections Program, CDC)
programme_institution_raw: CDC Emerging Infections Program (Georgia, Maryland, Oregon, Tennessee)
sources_raw: C1: Candida-positive blood cultures of residents of the surveillance area
species_id_raw: Luminex or D1/D2 sequencing (2012-2014); MALDI-TOF (2015-2016) at CDC
ast_method_raw: CLSI broth microdilution (fluconazole, voriconazole, anidulafungin, caspofungin, micafungin); E-test for amphotericin B

extraction_notes: 292 C. tropicalis cases (Table 5; by site: Georgia 120, Maryland 107, Oregon 17, Tennessee 48); 289 isolates sent to CDC with susceptibility (Table 6), stratified by year. title: In vitro susceptibility of Candida species to four antifungal agents assessed by the reference broth microdilution method.
ft_screening_reason: Meets general rule and IC8 (CLSI M27-A3/M27-S3; MIC by species)
setting_raw: university hospital (Faculty of Medicine, Gaziantep University); 35% from ICU
programme_institution_raw: Faculty of Medicine Hospital, Gaziantep University
sources_raw: C1: blood cultures of hospitalised patients
population_raw: hospitalised patients (ICU, paediatric oncology, internal medicine, others)
species_id_raw: germ tube, cornmeal-Tween 80 agar, Candida ID 2 chromogenic, API ID 32C
breakpoint_type_raw: clinical CBP (M27-S3); amphotericin B R >1 µg/mL (author's criterion)
extraction_notes: Only 3 C. tropicalis; Table 2 verified in the PDF. title: Prognostic factors of Candida spp. bloodstream infection in adults: A nine-year retrospective cohort study across tertiary hospitals in Brazil and Spain.

region_city_raw: São Paulo (2 hospitals), Porto Alegre, Curitiba (Brazil); Madrid (Spain)
sources_raw: C1: peripheral blood cultures of adults with candidaemia
species_id_raw: phenotypic (ID32C) in a reference laboratory (Brazil), phenotypic in Spain; MALDI-TOF MS in the last years in both countries

title: Species Distribution of Candidemia and Their Susceptibility in a Single Japanese University Hospital: Prior Micafungin Use Affects the Appearance of Candida parapsilosis and Elevation of Micafungin MICs in Non-parapsilosis Candida Species.
ft_screening_reason: Meets general rule and IC8 (CLSI M27-A3; MIC distribution by species)
design_raw: retrospective cross-sectional (series of blood isolates with clinical data)
sources_raw: C1: blood cultures (including central venous catheter)
population_raw: hospitalised patients with candidaemia (haematology, internal medicine, surgery, others)
ast_method_raw: commercial broth microdilution (yeast-like fungi DP-Eiken) according to CLSI M27-A3
interp_version_raw: M27-A3; M60 1st ed. (only for the micafungin criterion >0.06)
breakpoint_type_raw: of the author (micafungin >0.06 µg/mL); S/SDD/I/R categories calculated by the extractor with CLSI M60 1st ed. CBP and CLSI M59 ECV
azole_exposure_raw: Prior exposure (14 days) in non-parapsilosis: fluconazole 2, itraconazole 2, voriconazole 1 of 108; antifungal prophylaxis in 95.5% of haematology; not disaggregated by species
extraction_notes: Table 4 (MIC distribution by isolate) flattened in the Markdown without the C. tropicalis row; extracted from the PDF (pdftotext text coordinates). The authors do not categorise S/R for C. tropicalis; the categories are derived by the extractor. Caspofungin tested in only 7 of 11 C. tropicalis. No C. tropicalis with micafungin >0.06.

title: Antibiotic exposure as a risk factor for fluconazole-resistant Candida bloodstream infection.
ft_screening_reason: Meets general rule and IC8 (revised CLSI breakpoints written out)
setting_raw: 18 medical centres (75% of the country's hospital beds)
region_city_raw: national (Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Haifa, Petah Tikva and others)
population_raw: patients of all ages with candidaemia (97.8% nosocomial)
interp_document_raw: revised CLSI breakpoints for fluconazole (Pfaller et al. 2010)
interp_version_raw: revised CLSI CBP 2010 (S ≤2, SDD 4, R ≥8 for species other than C. glabrata and C. krusei)
azole_exposure_raw: Systemic antifungal in the previous 30 days in 63/444 patients (fluconazole 56); triazole exposure was associated with fluconazole resistance; not disaggregated by species
extraction_notes: 450 isolates from 444 patients (episodes by species out of 444). C. tropicalis R to fluconazole 5/74 (6.7%). SDD not broken down by species (16 SDD in total). Only fluconazole tested.

title: Candidemia in Brazilian neonatal intensive care units: risk factors, epidemiology, and antifungal resistance.
journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
ft_screening_reason: Meets general rule and IC8 (CLSI M27-A3/M60-Ed2; individual MICs)
programme_institution_raw: 3 neonatal ICUs in Pernambuco; Universidade Federal de Pernambuco
sources_raw: C1: blood cultures of neonates with suspected sepsis
population_raw: neonates (<28 days) in neonatal ICUs, mostly preterm and of very low weight
species_id_raw: classical phenotypic, Vitek 2, MALDI-TOF MS; ITS sequencing when needed
interp_document_raw: CLSI M27-A3; CLSI M60; CLSI M59
breakpoint_type_raw: clinical CBP (M60); ECV for amphotericin B
azole_exposure_raw: not recorded by species; the neonate with C. tropicalis was treated with amphotericin B; all exposed to broad-spectrum antibiotics

title: Risk factors for fluconazole-resistant candidemia.
ft_screening_reason: Meets general rule and IC8 (CLSI M44-A2 breakpoints)
setting_raw: tertiary university hospital (Virgen del Rocío); 94 episodes in ICU
breakpoint_type_raw: clinical CBP (S ≤8; SDD 16-32 grouped with R; R ≥16 according to the authors)
azole_exposure_raw: Prior fluconazole exposure (≥48 h) assessed; independent risk factor for fluconazole-resistant candidaemia; not disaggregated by species
extraction_notes: 229 episodes; 226 with susceptibility. C. tropicalis 37 (Table 1). 2 'resistant' C. tropicalis (MIC ≥16), a category that includes SDD. Fluconazole only.

title: Antifungal susceptibility of 205 Candida spp. isolated primarily during invasive Candidiasis and comparison of the Vitek 2 system with the CLSI broth microdilution and Etest methods.
ft_screening_reason: Meets general rule and IC8 (CLSI M27-A3/M27-A2; MIC and categories by species)
design_raw: experimental with clinical isolates (susceptibility method comparison)
setting_raw: university hospitals (CHU de Nîmes and Montpellier)
programme_institution_raw: CHU de Nîmes and CHU de Montpellier
sources_raw: C1: isolates from candidiasis (blood 81, sterile sites 62, deep pulmonary 51, multicolonised 14); not disaggregated by species
population_raw: patients with candidiasis, mainly invasive, all treated with antifungals
species_id_raw: chromogenic medium, Vitek 2 YST or ID32C
ast_method_raw: CLSI broth microdilution (reference), Vitek 2 AST-YS01 and E-test
breakpoint_type_raw: clinical CBP (fluconazole S ≤8, SDD 16-32, R ≥64; voriconazole S ≤1, SDD 2, R ≥4)
extraction_notes: 208 isolates tested, 205 analysed. Mixed sources not separated by species. The CLSI reference method at 48 h is extracted; Vitek 2 and E-test also 100% S for C. tropicalis. Amphotericin B (Table 3, verified in the PDF): internal inconsistency (100% ≤1 but 48 h range 0.5-2 and MIC90 2).
